Fixing Call of Duty: Inside Activision’s Modern Warfare 4 comeback plan
Plus, Lucasfilm Games targets independent studios for future Star Wars games
Christopher Dring
11 hours ago
Listen now on Apple , Spotify or YouTube
In This Edition,
State of Call of Duty
Activision’s comeback plan
LucasFilm targets independents
Plus! Lots of AI news
Hello there!
It’s a mega edition of The Game Business this week, featuring two huge interviews.
Our big focus is on Activision’s bid to regain fan trust with this year’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, featuring insight from chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl.
And we also have an interview with Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly and Fuse Games boss Matt Webster to discuss a more independent approach to making Star Wars games.
You can watch or listen to the whole thing above. Alternatively, I’ve picked out the key quotes below.
P.S. If you happen to be in London next week, The Game Business will be hosting a live on-stage interview with video game legend John Romero. It’s part of MCM Comic-Con, and game industry people can come for free by signing up for here.
Can Modern Warfare 4 fix Call of Duty?
By its own high standards, Call of Duty is in a tough spot.
Last year’s Black Ops 7 disappointed fans, and reached commercial lows not seen for nearly two decades. In Europe, the game’s launch was 50% below the previous year’s title. Meanwhile in the US, it finished the year at No.5, the lowest ranking for a Call of Duty since 2008’s World at War.
In fact, Battlefield 6 was the best-selling shooter of 2025, ending Call of Duty’s reign that had stretched back to the mid-2000s.
There’s also been a drop in players across the franchise. According to Ampere, the Call of Duty monthly player count was routinely around 40 million in 2024, while in 2026, the figures have been in the mid-20 million range (note: Modern Warfare 2 and 3 data is missing after July 2025, and Black Ops 6 data is missing after July 2026).
Note: Modern Warfare 2 and 3 data unavailable from July 2025 and Black Ops 6 data unavailable from July 2026
“I don’t think we were happy with every aspect of last year’s game, and we heard the feedback loud and clear,” Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl told The Game Business Show .
“With Modern Warfare 4, we’ve tried to adjust based on that feedback. It’s getting back to a grounded military shooter. Making it cinematic, making it authentic, and bringing that edge back that Call of Duty is known for.”
There is positive buzz around next week’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. And the series saw a surprising surge in players during the summer following the PlayStation ports of 2010’s Call of Duty: Black Ops and 2012’s Black Ops 2, which, according to Ampere, saw the franchise player count return to the near 40 million mark.
In our interview with Bahl, we discuss Call of Duty’s comeback plan, its new relationship with Game Pass, leaving behind PS4 and Xbox One, returning to Nintendo, dealing with GTA 6, and the surprise success of those Black Ops ports.
Sponsored Message
What does it take to make the highest-rated Star Wars game in 20 years? For Fuse Games, it meant building worlds worthy of a galaxy far, far away that hold up at breakneck speed.
Get an inside look at development as Fuse Games shares how Unreal Engine 5 helped the team deliver cinematic environments in Star Wars: Galactic Racer without sacrificing frame rate or fluid controls.
Read more here.
The Call of Duty comeback plan
Modern Warfare 4 at Fantastic Fest in New York
In 2022, Activision released Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, and in 2023 followed that up with Modern Warfare 3. It repeated the same ‘quick sequel’ approach with Black Ops 6 in 2024 and Black Ops 7 in 2025.
“It was not something that our community was looking for,” Bahl said. “They wanted something fresh, and even though there were different time settings, and ways to play the game with new features, that tonal shift is something that they were looking for. So, we’ve already stated that a future title is going to be a new sub-franchise and we’ve already laid the groundwork. But we’re really excited about Modern Warfare 4, and that addresses some of that feedback.”
Modern Warfare 4 will be more grounded, Bahl said. And the main success metric isn’t sales or player count, but whether fans care about the game.
“We’re not really holding ourselves to a specific number,” he says. “It’s more about living up to those expectations that we set out at the beginning of the year. And if that works, we can go from this game to the next game and build on that foundation. But it’s about getting that right first before thinking about anything else. Because even if it delivers on sales, if people don’t like the game, we’ve missed the mark.”
Bahl says there’s a bigger focus on community this time, and points to the From the Ward YouTube series, which takes fans behind-the-scenes on making Modern Warfare 4.
“There was a period where Call of Duty was a little hands-off and not talking to the community. And Infinity Ward, with the new leadership, has done a lot to really engage.”
This includes going to shows, with the game being shown at over 20 events worldwide.
“We had four different booths at Gamescom. We were absolutely everywhere. Coming out of last year, we really wanted to rebuild trust, and the best way you can do that is put the game in people’s hands.”
Activision eyes nostalgia
In the summer, Activision surprise launched Call of Duty: Black Ops 1 and 2 on PlayStation 4 and 5. The 2010 and 2012 games sold in huge numbers, and caught the publisher by surprise.
“We are definitely leaning into the nostalgia of playing with your friends,” Bahl told us. “The Black Ops ports were huge successes. We thought they would do well, we didn’t think they would do that well. But you can see that pent-up demand of being able to get back to the good old days of playing with your friends on a Friday night and having fun. MW4 does that.”
He added: “We took a lot of learnings from [those ports] and are starting to apply them to not only this game, but future games.”
Call of Duty’s press challenge
In a recent media roundtable, one prominent game journalist told me they don’t cover Call of Duty as much as they used to. He told me a lot of the franchise’s coverage comes from the influencer space.
Is that true?
“We get the coverage,” Bahl said. “But we call it the Call of Duty tax, when we’re thinking about the reviews or the reception. There’s obviously a lot of fandom around indie games and excitement around new games popping up every day on Steam. And Call of Duty’s been here for a very long time, and with that people sometimes forget that there’s so much work that goes into making these games. There’s 4,500 employees here that are trying to make the best possible experience.
“We have 100 million free-to-play players, we’ve sold 500 million units, it’s one of the biggest franchises of all time, and we have a billion downloads on mobile. And so that huge audience. I think, sometimes, gets overlooked or just becomes status quo. There’s craft that goes into these games, and the dedication from the teams was something that we wanted to show this year with the marketing.”
GTA 6 could boost Modern Warfare 4 sales
Last month, we suggested that GTA 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake could be video games’ ‘Barbenheimer’ moment. Activision challenges that idea, and is optimistic the upcoming Rockstar epic will drive some players to Call of Duty.
“Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year. And more people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and playing again, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall.
“And at the end of the day, what makes Call of Duty last the test of time is the community and social experience. When we look at our research and say, ‘what is the most exciting things about our games? Is it the gunplay?’ It’s actually spending time with friends. And so, we stand on our own [in that regard].
“If more people are talking about games, if there’s more press around it, that’s going to be good for everybody, not just us.”
Nintendo is fully behind Modern Warfare 4
Modern Warfare 4 is coming to Switch 2, which represents Call of Duty’s return to Nintendo for the first time since 2013.
“We’re rebuilding this relationship,” Bahl said. “Nintendo has been all in. We have a co-marketing campaign that we’ve launched with them. In a lot of ways, they want to age up their customer and want a broader spectrum by having an first person shooter on there. Their console sales grew to a certain point, but then stagnated, and this will allow them to extend the offering.
“I see it as a companion experience. I have a Switch 2, I’m flying to London this afternoon, and I’ll bring my Switch 2 with me and can play Modern Warfare 4. That’s an awesome companion experience.”
He added: “Nintendo’s been an amazing partner in co-marketing. I only see that relationship developing as we have future titles like Spyro coming back.”
Call of Duty’s future is about innovation
“I don’t want to give any spoilers, but this is going to be the epic conclusion of this recent series of Modern Warfare,” Bahl concluded. “It’s not that some characters and pieces can’t live on beyond this and be reinvented. But we’re excited by closing this chapter and launching a new one.
“Where we go with future games, we have to innovate. What we heard from the audience is they want new or better or different. The landscape is changing right under our feet. You’re seeing new games being built overnight, and you’re seeing tastes change and how people want to play.”
Check out the full interview with Bahl above.
You don’t have to be a Top Five publisher to make a Star Wars game
The success of Star Wars: Zero Company and Galactic Racer proves that you don’t need to be a giant game maker to deliver a hit Star Wars game.
Fuse Games’ Galactic Racer is the highest rated Star Wars game in 20 years, while Bit Reactor’s Zero Company is the joint second highest-rated title. Both games are notable for being made by independent studios.
“ It very much is part of the strategy,” said Lucasfilm Games VP Douglas Reilly in today’s The Game Business Show .
“Obviously, huge triple-A games like Battlefront are always going to be an essential part of the strategy. But one of the great things about Star Wars is it has all kinds of other opportunities to tell stories in different genres. The goal has been to find the best partner who makes that experience come alive inside the galaxy far, far away. And it doesn’t have to always be triple-A, sometimes it can be double-A, and it’s really about the experience that we’re delivering and the fantasy we’re fulfilling.”
Reilly told us that he’s learnt that if Lucasfilm can find the best partners to make Star Wars games, then the business side tends to work itself out. And sometimes those partners aren’t so obvious.
“ We’ve tried to be more flexible about who we’re willing to take pitches from,” he explained. “Good ideas can come from a lot of different places. You don’t have to necessarily be a Top Five publisher to make a great Star Wars game. There are some hurdles. We have a high quality bar, and that means typically we work with more experienced teams than ones with no track record. But we’re exploring all kinds of things, large and small, with partners that are going to surprise folks.”
“We’re exploring all kinds of things, large and small, with partners that are going to surprise folks”
Indeed, although they are independent teams, Bit Reactor is made up of veteran developers from the XCOM series, while Fuse was founded by Criterion leaders who had worked with Lucasfilm before on Battlefront.
Fuse boss Matt Webster said that Lucasfilm is more than just a licensing partner, and advises other studios to adapt to that.
“You have to build that into your way of working,” he said. “It’s like any other constraint. You can’t fight it. You’re working with it. And it’s an honor and a privilege to do so. They are the experts in Star Wars, and there are game makers there, and that’s incredibly valuable. I’ve worked with other license partners in the past, and it’s an approval transaction model. This is not that, by any stretch of the imagination.
“If you want to be making something with somebody else’s property, and particularly such a beloved thing as Star Wars, there’s a responsibility to that. You need to operate accordingly.”
That’s it for today’s bumper edition of The Game Business Show. Join us next week for more major interviews!

title: 2026日本数字广告市场洞察
author: Sensor Tower
text:
日本数字广告市场持续扩张。2026年1–8月，Sensor Tower 追踪渠道内数字广告支出达到 93亿美元，同比增长22% ，广告展示量达到 2.6万亿次，同比增长8% 。
增长背后，日本市场的渠道与行业结构也进一步分化：Instagram 等社交平台承接更高预算，LINE 凭借低 CPM 提供规模化曝光；媒体与娱乐继续成为最大的广告行业，而 AI 搜索、大型体育赛事等新场景，则正在打开新的消费者触达机会。
Sensor Tower 最新发布的《2026年日本市场数字广告投放洞察》基于 Pathmatics 数字广告洞察，并结合应用表现、网站及受众数据，深入解析日本广告市场、渠道、重点行业及头部品牌的最新投放趋势。
日本数字广告支出同比增长22%，渠道分工进一步清晰
日本数字广告市场的增长伴随着渠道结构的进一步分化。在 Sensor Tower 追踪的广告渠道中，LINE 的广告展示量位居第一，Instagram 和 Facebook 紧随其后；Google、NAVER 和 Recruit Holdings 则位列广告展示量头部广告主。
但预算与曝光并不完全同步：Instagram 占日本数字广告支出的 36% ，是预算最集中的渠道；LINE 虽仅占9%的广告支出，却贡献了 39%的广告展示次数 ，推算平均 CPM 约为0.9美元。由此，日本市场正在形成更加明确的渠道分工： LINE 承担规模化曝光，社交与视频平台则获得更高的预算密度。
完整报告进一步拆解 Instagram、LINE、TikTok、YouTube 等渠道的支出、展示量及 CPM 差异。
下载免费报告
AI搜索进入消费者决策链路，高意向场景率先释放广告价值
随着 AI 搜索逐渐融入消费者的信息获取、比较与决策过程，品牌也获得了新的触点。
Sensor Tower 数据显示，在日本市场， 房地产、旅游、金融服务和求职教育等决策型行业对 ChatGPT 广告渠道表现出更强亲和度 。与传统社交广告更偏广泛触达不同，AI 搜索呈现出更加明显的搜索、比较和规划场景特征。
在8月盂兰盆节前夕，旅行、购物等与假期消费相关的品牌也开始加大 ChatGPT 渠道的营销投入。AI 搜索的价值因此不仅在于增加新的曝光渠道，更在于触达正处于主动研究和决策阶段的用户。
这种变化已经体现在具体品牌策略中。PERSOL CAREER 旗下高端转职平台 doda X 在2026年7–8月已有 11%的广告展示来自 ChatGPT ，高于求职与教育行业整体水平，体现出品牌正在根据目标人群和决策场景尝试不同的媒体组合。
内容消费驱动日本广告市场，漫画与流媒体形成鲜明本土特色
与全球整体市场不同，日本数字广告支出和展示量最大的行业均为媒体与娱乐。
2026年1–8月，该行业数字广告支出同比增长23%，展示量同比增长14%。其中，图书与漫画是最大的广告展示子品类，同比增长22%；电影与电视节目、社交媒体广告展示量也分别同比增长35%和51%。
NAVER Webtoon、Piccoma等漫画平台持续占据头部广告主位置，AbemaTV、U-NEXT、Disney+ 等流媒体平台同样活跃，日本数字广告竞争因此呈现出鲜明的本土内容消费特色。
中国出海游戏呈现多品类布局日本市场
日本仍然是全球游戏发行商重点争夺的核心市场之一。2024年以来，日本游戏品牌数字广告投入整体保持上升趋势，中国、韩国及欧美发行商均持续加大营销投入。
值得关注的是，2026年1–8月，日本游戏广告展示量 Top 10 中已有多款中国出海产品上榜，包括《明日方舟：终末地》、《Puzzles & Survival》、《Gossip Harbor: Merge & Story》和《信长之野望 真战》。
上榜产品覆盖 RPG、策略、合成休闲及社交娱乐等多个类型，显示中国游戏厂商在日本市场的营销布局正在从传统重度游戏向更多内容和用户场景延伸。
从“多投广告”到“投对广告”
随着日本数字广告支出持续增长，品牌不仅需要扩大市场触达，也开始更加注重渠道、人群、内容与营销节点之间的协同。
例如，麒麟针对旗下不同产品线采取差异化渠道策略：饮料业务在 TikTok 上拥有更高曝光占比，更积极触达年轻消费者；健康与美护业务则更偏向 YouTube，以适应测评、种草和长视频内容消费场景。进入夏季与 FIFA 世界杯期间，麒麟又根据产品季节性和赛事
节点动态切换饮料与啤酒业务的投放重点。
这也反映出日本数字广告市场的变化： 增长机会越来越来自“渠道 × 用户 × 场景”的精准匹配，而不仅仅是预算规模本身。
